name: Jerusalem
summary: Jerusalem is among the oldest cities on Earth and holy to three faiths. A Canaanite town became King David's capital around 1000 BC and the site of Solomon's Temple; that Temple was destroyed by Babylon, rebuilt, and destroyed again by Rome in AD 70, leaving the Western Wall. Christians revere it as the place of the Crucifixion and Resurrection, Muslims as the site of the Dome of the Rock and al-Aqsa. Fought over by Crusaders, Ayyubids and Ottomans, it remains one of the world's most contested cities — its status disputed to this day.

events.title: Canaanite Jerusalem
events.body: A Canaanite town called Urusalim appears in Egyptian records.

events.title: David’s capital
events.body: King David takes the city and makes it the capital of Israel.

events.title: Solomon’s Temple
events.body: Solomon builds the First Temple on Mount Moriah.

events.title: Assyria repelled
events.body: Hezekiah’s Jerusalem survives an Assyrian siege; his water tunnel still runs beneath the city.

events.title: Babylon destroys the Temple
events.body: Nebuchadnezzar razes the city and Temple and exiles the people of Judah.

events.title: The Second Temple
events.body: Returned exiles rebuild the Temple.

events.title: The Maccabees
events.body: The Maccabean revolt frees Jerusalem and rededicates the Temple, remembered at Hanukkah.

events.title: Herod the Great
events.body: Herod rebuilds the Temple on a vast scale and fortifies the city.

events.title: The Crucifixion
events.body: By Christian tradition Jesus is crucified and buried in Jerusalem.

events.title: Rome destroys the Temple
events.body: Titus sacks Jerusalem and burns the Second Temple, leaving only its retaining wall.

events.title: Aelia Capitolina
events.body: After the Bar Kokhba revolt Rome rebuilds the city as pagan Aelia Capitolina and bars Jews from it.

events.title: The Holy Sepulchre
events.body: Constantine’s mother Helena builds the Church of the Holy Sepulchre over the tomb of Christ.

events.title: The Muslim conquest
events.body: The Caliph Umar takes Jerusalem peacefully from Byzantium.

events.title: The Dome of the Rock
events.body: The Umayyads build the Dome of the Rock on the Temple Mount.

events.title: The Crusaders
events.body: The First Crusade storms Jerusalem in a notorious massacre and founds a Latin kingdom.

events.title: Saladin retakes the city
events.body: Saladin recaptures Jerusalem for Islam after the Battle of Hattin.

events.title: Ottoman rule
events.body: The Ottomans take Jerusalem; it stays under their rule for four centuries.

events.title: Süleyman’s walls
events.body: Süleyman the Magnificent rebuilds the Old City walls that still stand today.

events.title: Beyond the walls
events.body: The first neighbourhoods are built outside the crowded Old City.

events.title: General Allenby enters
events.body: British forces take Jerusalem from the Ottomans in the First World War.

events.title: The UN partition vote
events.body: The United Nations votes to partition Palestine, proposing Jerusalem as an international city.

events.title: A divided city
events.body: War splits Jerusalem between Israel and Jordan.

events.title: The Six-Day War
events.body: Israel captures the Old City and East Jerusalem.

events.title: Israel’s declaration
events.body: Israel declares a united Jerusalem its capital — a status not recognised by most of the world.

events.title: The Second Intifada
events.body: Tensions on the Temple Mount help ignite a Palestinian uprising.

places.name: Temple Mount / Haram al-Sharif
places.note: Site of the Jewish Temples and of the Dome of the Rock and al-Aqsa.

places.name: The Western Wall
places.note: The surviving retaining wall of Herod’s Temple Mount.

places.name: Church of the Holy Sepulchre
places.note: Built over the traditional site of Christ’s tomb.

places.name: City of David
places.note: The oldest settled core, south of the Temple Mount.

places.name: The Old City walls
places.note: The present walls, rebuilt by Süleyman the Magnificent.

caveats: This timeline is compiled from general reference works — listed under Sources — rather than an event-by-event archive of primary documents, as the Mumbai timeline is. Treat it as a reliable outline, not a citation of record.
Dates for the earliest, legendary events are traditional rather than documented.
Jerusalem’s political status and boundaries are internationally disputed; this account records widely agreed history as neutrally as it can, and takes no position on any claim.

list.name: The House of David
list.legacy: The First Temple and a central place in three faiths
list.summary: David and Solomon made Jerusalem their capital and built the First Temple; the line runs deep through Jewish and Christian tradition.

list.name: The Hasmoneans
list.summary: The Maccabees and their heirs, who freed Jerusalem and rededicated the Temple.

list.name: The Herodian dynasty
list.legacy: The Temple Mount whose Western Wall still stands
list.summary: Herod the Great rebuilt the Temple and its mount on a monumental scale.

list.name: Kings of Jerusalem
list.summary: The Latin rulers of the Crusader kingdom centred on the holy city.
